title: Efficient Market Hypothesis
text: Markets reflect available information. Hard to consistently beat the market.

title: Behavioral finance
text: Studies how biases affect financial decisions. Emotions can drive irrational trades.

title: Loss aversion
text: Investors dislike losses more than they like gains. Leads to holding losers too long.

title: Overconfidence bias
text: Believing too strongly in one’s skill causes excessive trading and risk.

title: Anchoring bias
text: Fixating on past prices or numbers when making new decisions.

title: Herd behavior
text: Copying what others do in markets, often during bubbles or crashes.

title: Time value of money
text: A dollar today is worth more than a dollar tomorrow due to earning potential.

title: Compound interest
text: Interest earns more interest over time. The longer invested, the greater the effect.

title: Capital Asset Pricing Model
text: Estimates expected return based on risk-free rate, beta, and market risk premium.

title: Beta coefficient
text: Measures sensitivity to market movements. Beta >1 is more volatile.

title: Sharpe ratio
text: Risk-adjusted performance: excess return per unit of volatility.

title: Sortino ratio
text: Like Sharpe but only penalizes downside volatility.

title: Alpha generation
text: Performance above benchmark expectations. Difficult to sustain long-term.

title: Passive investing
text: Tracking indexes instead of picking stocks. Low cost and broad diversification.

title: Active investing
text: Selecting securities to outperform benchmarks. Requires research and skill.

title: Momentum investing
text: Buying assets that have been rising in price, assuming the trend continues.

title: Value investing
text: Buying undervalued companies based on fundamentals. Seeks margin of safety.

title: Growth investing
text: Investing in companies expected to grow earnings rapidly.

title: Dividend investing
text: Focusing on stocks with consistent dividends. Common among income seekers.

title: Quantitative investing
text: Uses models and algorithms to make data-driven decisions.

title: Market capitalization
text: Total company value = share price × shares outstanding.

title: Price-to-book ratio
text: Compares price to accounting book value per share.

title: Return on equity
text: Net income ÷ shareholders’ equity. Indicates profitability.

title: Debt-to-equity ratio
text: Measures leverage. Higher values mean more debt risk.

title: Earnings per share
text: Company profit divided by shares. Growth often drives price.

title: Free cash flow yield
text: Free cash flow ÷ market cap. Measures cash generation efficiency.

title: Discounted cash flow
text: Values company by estimating future cash flows discounted to present value.

title: Intrinsic value
text: True estimated worth of an asset based on fundamentals.

title: Rebalancing
text: Adjusting portfolio back to target allocation to control risk.

title: Risk-adjusted return
text: Return relative to risk taken. Higher indicates efficiency.

title: Liquidity risk
text: Inability to sell at fair value quickly. Common in thinly traded assets.

title: Inflation risk
text: Rising prices erode real returns.

title: Credit risk
text: Borrower may default on obligations.

title: Interest rate risk
text: Bond prices fall when interest rates rise.

title: Systematic risk
text: Market-wide risk that cannot be diversified away.

title: Unsystematic risk
text: Company or industry-specific risk that can be diversified.

title: Asset correlation
text: Degree to which assets move together. Lower correlation increases diversification.

title: Portfolio optimization
text: Mathematically balancing risk and return using diversification principles.

title: Expected return
text: Anticipated average gain or loss over time.

title: Standard deviation
text: Statistical measure of volatility or dispersion around mean return.

title: Covariance
text: Indicates how two assets move relative to each other.

title: Beta diversification
text: Combining assets with different market sensitivities to reduce volatility.

title: Efficient frontier
text: Set of portfolios offering highest return for given risk.

title: Modern portfolio theory
text: Mathematical framework optimizing risk-return tradeoff.

title: Black-Scholes model
text: Mathematical model for option pricing.

title: Put-call parity
text: Relationship between prices of puts, calls, and underlying assets.

title: Futures contracts
text: Agreements to buy/sell assets at set price in the future.

title: Hedging
text: Reducing risk exposure by taking offsetting positions.

title: Stop orders
text: Automated trades that execute once a price threshold is met.

title: Trailing stops
text: Move stop price along with gains to lock in profits.
